A1.justification: Both complete, readable 16-page PDFs describe the same PDFNet research. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and supplements support comparison despite substantial rewriting, renaming, and reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original DIS-5K comparisons and ablations in Tables 1–5, plus HRSOD/UHRSD experiments in supplementary Table A2.

after.justification: v4 retains and revises these empirical results and adds depth-variance analysis, additional controls, foundation-model comparisons, and failure cases.

M1.justification: The overall architecture and 8×8 patch strategy remain, but FSE changes from continuous amplified boundary responses and averaged patch scores to thresholded binary boundaries and any-boundary patch selection, with revised feature gating (v1 Equations 2–5; v4 Equations 2–7). The reported auxiliary depth-supervision sum expands from four to five stages. Averaging the integrity loss is offset by removing its outer half-weight, preserving that contribution's effective weight.

E1.justification: Both versions use DIS-5K and the HRSOD/UHRSD training and test sets. The latter experiments already appear in v1 Appendix F and move to v4 Supplement (5). Added comparisons and analyses use existing coverage; ground-truth box prompts are an added comparator protocol, not a new dataset or target task.

E2.justification: v4 retains the original benchmark comparators but adds RGB-depth-concatenated MVANet* to Table 1 and SAM, HQ-SAM, and Pi-SAM to supplementary Table 10. Its patch-count comparison also adds MVANet configurations with 2×2, 3×3, and 4×4 patches (Table 4), whereas v1 Table 5 evaluates only PDFNet configurations.

E3.justification: New evaluation designs include ground-truth-derived box prompts for foundation models, with/without pre-metric binarization, and separate all-ones replacements for the S and Bd controls. v1 exempts FP-DIS and DiffDIS from its standardized 1024×1024 evaluation by using published scores; v4 states that all models are tested at that resolution. This is a reported protocol revision, not proof that every experiment was rerun. The principal dataset splits and 100-epoch training budget remain.

E4.justification: Beyond retained depth-quality, loss, and patch-count ablations, v4 adds dataset-level foreground/background depth-variance analysis (Figure 1), separate integrity and boundary controls (Table 2), direct MVANet patch-density tests (Table 4), loss-transfer tests on MAGNet and DACOD (Table 6), a binarization study (Table 8), and concrete failure cases (Figure 12). These substantially expand tests of the method's motivation, components, and limitations.

E5.justification: v4 Figure 1 adds descriptive statistical reporting through density curves and box plots of depth variance across DIS-TR foreground, background, and full-image regions; v1's corresponding motivation figure contains qualitative examples only. These summarize data distributions and dispersion, not experimental uncertainty. Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or formal significance tests.

E6.justification: Many existing scores change alongside substantial new results. In Table 1, PDFNet's DIS-TE (ALL) values change from 0.925/0.874/0.943/0.915/0.031 to 0.915/0.876/0.944/0.916/0.030 for maximum F-measure, weighted F-measure, E-measure, structural measure, and MAE. Its HRSOD/UHRSD maximum F-measures change from 0.971/0.970 to 0.965/0.963 (v1 Table A2; v4 Table 9). Comparator scores, ablations, and efficiency results also change. These are reported revisions, not established same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: FSE's mathematical definitions change substantively: v4 introduces binary threshold and existential patch-selection predicates in place of continuous responses and averaged scores. The depth-supervision summation also changes its stage count. Neither version supplies theorems or proofs, and the compensating integrity-loss rescaling does not constitute a new mathematical objective.

C1.justification: The central depth-prior, fine-patch, and competitive-accuracy contributions remain. v4 emphasizes resolving the accuracy–efficiency trade-off and broadens one introductory contribution from using less than 11% of diffusion models' parameters to less than 11% of their computational cost. That is a stronger resource claim, although the abstract retains the parameter-based wording.

C2.justification: v4 introduces binarization as a possible explanation for metric differences with DiffDIS, interprets the loss-transfer experiments, and discusses foundation models' boundary weaknesses. It also explicitly identifies failures involving ultra-fine detail and erroneous monocular depth, suggesting higher resolution or better depth generators (Supplement (9), Figure 12). These add substantive explanations and applicability boundaries absent from v1.

D1.justification: v4 adds baseline backbone specifications and identifies ImageNet-21K pretraining more precisely than v1's generic ImageNet description. It documents new gating thresholds and ablation controls. Conversely, v1's explicit statement that training uses randomly selected depth qualities is omitted. Hardware, optimizer, learning rate, batch size, training duration, and depth-generation pipelines remain documented, and both versions identify the same code repository.

R1.justification: v4 adds references and discussion for SAM, HQ-SAM, Pi-SAM, and several backbone architectures, while removing the JL-DCF reference. It credits diffusion methods' strong generative priors and emphasizes their computational expense, refining v1's broader criticism of previous methods' dependence on local features. The three principal related-work areas remain DIS, monocular depth, and depth-aware dense prediction.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work, and much of the method and experimental prose are extensively rewritten around an accuracy–efficiency narrative. The title changes, and PDFNet expands to Prior of Depth Fusion Network instead of Patch-Depth Fusion Network. Main headings lose numbering, ablation subsections are reordered, and lettered appendices become reorganized numbered supplementary sections.

P2.justification: v4 adds statistical plots to the motivation figure, redraws the conceptual comparison and pipeline diagrams, revises the FSE diagram, and introduces a failure-case figure. Tables gain backbone, control, metric, and efficiency information, with new loss-transfer, binarization, and foundation-model tables. Existing qualitative panels are retained but relocated and resized within a substantially revised layout.

improvement.justification: v4 better substantiates the depth prior and component contributions through dataset-level variance evidence, stronger controls, and loss-transfer tests, while making failure conditions explicit. These improve the paper's explanatory value. The gains are tempered by unexplained score revisions, apparently duplicated RISNet entries across different subsets in Table 1, and a broader computational-cost claim that the parameter ratio does not establish. The net improvement is useful but limited.
